clue.text: It brings a lump to one's throat

definitions.text: It brings a lump to one's throat

blocks.clueFragment: It brings a lump to one's throat
blocks.note: surface reading: something so moving that it makes you choke up with emotion
setter's reading: the thing that literally forms a bump at the front of the neck

explanation.surface: A tear-jerking film or song that leaves someone choked with emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'a lump in the throat' means being moved; here the lump is a physical one, the projection of the larynx.
explanation.definitionFit: The visible bulge of cartilage at the front of a man's neck is the laryngeal prominence, popularly named after the biblical first man.

clue.text: Flying is not yet fully developed

blocks.note: first meaning: airborne, aloft like a plane
second meaning: undecided, still being planned

explanation.surface: A remark that an aircraft design is still a prototype.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both airborne and, idiomatically, uncertain or unsettled, as plans that remain undecided.

clue.text: A fine state to be in

definitions.text: A fine state to be in

blocks.clueFragment: A fine state to be in
blocks.note: surface reading: an ironic exclamation about a mess, or a pleasant country to live in
setter's reading: the condition named in the idiom 'in fine ___', meaning in good shape

explanation.surface: An exasperated remark about a muddle, or praise for a pleasant place.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is almost only met in the phrase 'in fine fettle', so the clue supplies both 'fine' and 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means condition or shape, especially good health, and survives mainly in the set idiom with 'fine'.

clue.text: The last piece of music to be accepted by disco dancers?

indicators.note: what is accepted is taken in and held, so the answer sits inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Wondering which closing track a disco crowd will put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: In music theory the closing passage that rounds off a movement is called by this Italian term meaning tail.

clue.text: Inspectors' appraisal fools people, in a way

indicators.note: the people are placed in the way, enclosed by its letters

blocks.note: asses are fools
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
men are people

explanation.surface: A school inspection report rubbishing the staff as idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: The people go inside the way, so the second half is S-MEN-T.
explanation.definitionFit: An evaluation or judgment is what inspectors produce after examining something, so the word fits their appraisal.

clue.text: Sneak in late

blocks.note: taken as written
late in the sense of previous, as 'the late chairman'

explanation.surface: Slipping into a room quietly after arriving behind time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sneak in' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'Sneak' alone is a noun definition and 'in late' is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneak is a tell-tale who reports on others, just as a police informant passes on information.

clue.text: Refuse to acknowledge down is out

indicators.note: out as in out of order or out of place, so the preceding letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone won't admit a batsman is dismissed, or a player knocked down is out.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate or deny any connection with something, such as a relative, is to decline to recognise it.

clue.text: Leading estate agent's notice

indicators.note: the leading part of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
a secret agent is a spy

explanation.surface: A notice board put up by the top estate agency in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading estate agent' looks like one phrase, but only 'Leading estate' works together; 'agent' is separate, and 'notice' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch sight of something is to spot or observe it, the verb sense of notice.

clue.text: Relaxing one's guard is risky

indicators.note: relaxing loosens what was held tight, so the following letters come free and rearrange

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that letting your defences down invites trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a sound piece of advice, which hides that 'Relaxing' loosens the letters of the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hazardous or perilous carries a chance of harm, so it is a synonym of risky.

clue.text: Proverbially hard on one's toes?

blocks.note: surface reading: something that hurts your feet, like tight shoes
setter's reading: the things in the saying 'as hard as ___', which also grow on the ends of your toes

explanation.surface: A grumble about shoes or a sport that punishes the feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard on' suggests causing pain; really it means hard things sitting on the toes.
explanation.definitionFit: The horny plates at the tips of fingers and toes are proverbially tough, as in the simile 'hard as ___'.

clue.text: Mother repeatedly passes round hat for Asian dignitary

indicators.note: to pass round something is to go all the way about it, so the mothers wrap around the hat

blocks.note: MA is mother, said twice
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mum keeps passing the hat round, collecting for a visiting holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: The two mothers sit either side of the hat: MA-HAT-MA.
explanation.definitionFit: The title, meaning 'great soul', is given in India to a revered sage, most famously Gandhi.

clue.text: What's needed by firm in money trouble?

definitions.text: What's needed by firm in money trouble?

indicators.note: something in trouble is disturbed and upset, so its letters are thrown into disorder
the firm is put in the jumbled cash, sitting inside its letters

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking what a cash-strapped company must do.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and the firm goes into a jumble of the cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A business short of funds needs to cut spending, and careful thrift is exactly what the word means.

clue.text: Saw notice on time

blocks.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a notice about the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past tense of see; it is the noun meaning an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: An old saw is a well-worn proverb or maxim, the same thing as a traditional saying.

clue.text: The price of silence?

blocks.note: surface reading: a philosophical question about what keeping quiet costs you
setter's reading: an actual payment handed over to keep someone quiet

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds abstract or moral, but it means a literal sum paid to a blackmailer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bribe paid to stop someone revealing a secret is literally what buys their silence.

clue.text: Audience standing up, well-pleased with one's address

blocks.note: a theatre audience is the house, as in 'full house'
proud can mean projecting or standing up above a surface

explanation.surface: A standing ovation for a speaker delighted with their own speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' seems to be a speech, and the audience a standing ovation; really the address is where you live.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes great pride in keeping their home immaculate is pleased with where they live, their address.

clue.text: Yeasty reds drunk in the recent past

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about unsteadily, so these letters lurch into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cloudy red wines that were drunk not long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun means days gone by, the time just behind us, as in the song about all my troubles seeming far away.

clue.text: They are ready to drop by the time they have qualified

definitions.text: They are ready to drop by the time they have qualified

blocks.clueFragment: ready to drop by the time they have qualified
blocks.note: surface reading: students exhausted after gruelling training
setter's reading: soldiers trained and fit to jump from aircraft

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready to drop' means worn out in the surface but literally prepared to descend from a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers trained to be delivered into battle by jumping from aircraft are only cleared to do so after qualifying.

clue.text: Indian state capital

blocks.note: first meaning: a Native American people of the Great Plains
second meaning: the capital city of Wyoming

explanation.surface: The capital of a state in India.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to India, but the Indian is a Native American and the state a US one.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a Plains tribe and to the city in the US that serves as Wyoming's seat of government.

clue.text: Instrument to stamp fine material

blocks.note: an organ is a musical instrument
a die is a tool for stamping coins or patterns

explanation.surface: A tool for pressing a pattern into delicate fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' looks like a tool, but it is the musical kind.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a thin, stiff, sheer cotton muslin, a delicate fabric used for dresses and trimmings.

clue.text: Running away to join up?

blocks.note: surface reading: a youngster who flees home to enlist in the army
setter's reading: a couple fleeing together to be joined in marriage

explanation.walkthrough: 'Join up' suggests enlisting, the classic reason for running away; here the joining is a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovers who flee secretly to marry without parental consent are said to run off together, which is this act.

clue.text: Carole's making an announcement

indicators.note: making as in being made into something new, so the name is refashioned from its own letters

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman named Carole is about to make a public statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' here means turning into: Carole's letters are made into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides a prophet, the word can mean the prophetic utterance itself, an authoritative pronouncement.

clue.text: Does it call for a costume ornament?

blocks.note: first meaning: a brass instrument that sounds military calls
second meaning: a tube-shaped glass bead sewn onto clothing

explanation.surface: Asking whether a fancy-dress outfit needs a decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call for' reads as 'require'; split it, and 'Does it call' describes a military horn.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the valveless brass horn used for reveille and a cylindrical bead used to trim dresses.

clue.text: Goes on the stage

blocks.note: first meaning: gets onto a ship, bus or train
second meaning: the theatre, as in 'treading the ___'

explanation.surface: An actor making an entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes on the stage' reads as one phrase about acting; it splits into a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for embarking on a vehicle and a plural noun used for the theatre stage.

clue.text: He gains nothing from his activities

definitions.text: He gains nothing from his activities

blocks.clueFragment: He gains nothing from his activities
blocks.note: surface reading: someone whose efforts are fruitless
setter's reading: one who takes no payment for his sport or pastime

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like a failure; it means someone who does it unpaid, for love.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pursues a sport or hobby without being paid, in contrast to a professional, earns nothing from it.

clue.text: Almost lost to charity

indicators.note: what is lost goes missing, so the letters of the small word that follows are dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters of this little word are the ones removed

explanation.surface: Something nearly given away to a good cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost to' reads as given to charity, but 'to' is what goes missing: take the O and T out of the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Money or food given to the poor is the traditional word for charitable gifts.

clue.text: In entering a new trade, one should be

definitions.text: In entering a new trade, one should be

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the first word is placed within the rearranged letters
a new version of a word is a remade one, so its letters are set out afresh

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice that someone starting a new job should have proper instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, completed by the missing word, while the first word goes inside a rearranged 'trade'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone taking up a new occupation ought to have been taught the necessary skills, that is, schooled and qualified.

clue.text: One may win it by a head

definitions.text: One may win it by a head

blocks.clueFragment: One may win it by a head
blocks.note: surface reading: a racehorse winning a close finish
setter's reading: winning by calling the side of a spun coin correctly

explanation.walkthrough: 'By a head' sounds like a horse race margin; it is the heads side of a coin flipped before a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin flip decides, for example, who bats first, and calling heads correctly wins it.

clue.text: Fruit of the lemon variety

indicators.note: a variety is a different form of the same thing, so the same letters take another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fruit belonging to the citrus family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety' looks like a botanical type; it signals a different arrangement of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This large round fruit with sweet juicy flesh, such as a cantaloupe, is a familiar fruit.

clue.text: Useful expression for one raising a child

definitions.text: Useful expression for one raising a child

blocks.clueFragment: Useful expression for one raising a child
blocks.note: surface reading: a handy saying for parents bringing up children
setter's reading: lifting a little one up off the ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising a child' suggests parenting; here it means physically lifting a toddler, with the cheery exclamation that goes with it.
explanation.definitionFit: This playful exclamation is said when lifting a small child or helping someone up after a tumble.
